ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #9 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is a nonverbal cue that shows you are listening? (1 mark)
   A. Talking to a friend
   B. Looking out of the window
   C. Looking at the speaker and nodding
   D. Turning your back

2. Which is a polite way to interrupt a speaker? (1 mark)
   A. Be quiet!
   B. You are wrong!
   C. Stop talking!
   D. Excuse me, may I ask a question?

3. What is a factual text? (1 mark)
   A. A made-up story only
   B. A text that gives true information
   C. A poem only
   D. A joke

4. Which is NOT one of the five senses? (1 mark)
   A. sight
   B. smell
   C. taste
   D. sleep

5. Which is a better describing phrase than 'nice room'? (1 mark)
   A. a room
   B. a bright, tidy room
   C. the room, room
   D. a room room

6. Which word has the consonant cluster /sk/? (1 mark)
   A. goal
   B. race
   C. ball
   D. desk

7. Which word begins with the unvoiced sound /θ/? (1 mark)
   A. that
   B. thank
   C. they
   D. the

8. In which order do we read comic panels? (1 mark)
   A. Right to left
   B. Any order
   C. Left to right and top to bottom
   D. Bottom to top

9. After 'does' or 'did', which form of the main verb do we use? (1 mark)
   A. The base form
   B. The -ing form
   C. The plural form
   D. The past participle

10. Which question word asks about ownership? (1 mark)
   A. when
   B. whose
   C. where
   D. who

11. Which word begins with the cluster 'gr'? (1 mark)
   A. swim
   B. clap
   C. grass
   D. glass

12. How is a diary different from a letter? (1 mark)
   A. A diary has no date
   B. A diary always has an address
   C. A diary is written for yourself and is not sent
   D. A diary is always sent by post

13. In which person is a diary usually written? (1 mark)
   A. Third person (he, she)
   B. No person
   C. Second person (you)
   D. First person (I, we)

14. Which sentence uses the pattern 'very ... but ...' correctly? (1 mark)
   A. The shirt very nice but expensive.
   B. The shirt is but very nice, it is expensive.
   C. Very shirt is nice, but.
   D. The shirt is very nice, but it is too expensive.

15. Which word has a silent h? (1 mark)
   A. house
   B. help
   C. hand
   D. honest

16. How do newspapers and magazines usually differ? (1 mark)
   A. Magazines have no pictures
   B. Newspapers have no words
   C. Newspapers give news often; magazines give features less often with more pictures
   D. They are the same

17. Which preposition shows movement from one side to the other inside something, such as a gate? (1 mark)
   A. under
   B. near
   C. over
   D. through

18. What comes after a preposition in a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. A noun or pronoun
   B. Another preposition
   C. A question mark
   D. A full stop

19. Which is the correct spelling of the word that tells where you live? (1 mark)
   A. address
   B. adres
   C. addres
   D. adress

20. What is the -ing form of 'run'? (1 mark)
   A. runing
   B. running
   C. runnning
   D. runeing

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Draw a mind map in words: put 'Keeping Fit' in the centre and give four branches. (4 marks)

22. Give three words with silent letters and name the silent letter in each. (3 marks)

23. Make two sentences with 'very ... but ...' about shopping. (2 marks)

24. Write four sentences for a short speech about your favourite game. (4 marks)

25. Mark the words you would stress in: 'We must keep our compound clean.' (3 marks)

26. Explain the difference between a fact and an opinion. Give one example of each. (3 marks)

27. Give two words with /θ/ and two with /ð/. (4 marks)

28. Explain the meaning of 'tax' and 'fine'. (3 marks)

29. Write two words for each cluster: (a) br (b) gr. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #9 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Looking at the speaker and nodding
   Eye contact and nods show attention.

2. D — Excuse me, may I ask a question?
   It is polite because it asks permission.

3. B — A text that gives true information
   Factual texts share facts.

4. D — sleep
   The senses are sight, sound, smell, touch and taste.

5. B — a bright, tidy room
   Exact adjectives give a clearer picture.

6. D — desk
   'Desk' ends in sk.

7. B — thank
   'Thank' has the unvoiced 'th'.

8. C — Left to right and top to bottom
   We read a comic like a book.

9. A — The base form
   For example: 'When does she practise?'

10. B — whose
   'Whose' asks who owns something.

11. C — grass
   'Grass' begins with g and r.

12. C — A diary is written for yourself and is not sent
   A letter is sent to another person.

13. D — First person (I, we)
   A diary is about what I did and felt.

14. D — The shirt is very nice, but it is too expensive.
   It has 'very' + adjective, then 'but' with the difficulty.

15. D — honest
   'Honest' is said 'onest'.

16. C — Newspapers give news often; magazines give features less often with more pictures
   Newspapers are published often and carry news.

17. D — through
   'Through' shows movement within.

18. A — A noun or pronoun
   For example: 'on the table'.

19. A — address
   Address has a double d and a double s.

20. B — running
   Double the n.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Centre: Keeping Fit. Branches: exercise, healthy food, sleep, clean water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the centre and 1 for each branch.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: knee (k), debt (b), honest (h).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each word with its silent letter.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: The mango is very sweet, but it is small. The bag is very nice, but it is expensive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: A greeting, the name of the game, a reason, and a closing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: We must KEEP our COMpound CLEAN. (Important words: keep, compound, clean.)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each important word.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: A fact can be checked, for example 'Germs are tiny'. An opinion says what someone thinks, for example 'Cold water is nicest'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each definition and 1 for examples.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: /θ/: think, three, thank, mouth (any two). /ð/: this, that, the, mother (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tax is money paid to the government to help run the country. A fine is money paid as a punishment for breaking a rule or law.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for showing a difference.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: (a) bring, broom (or bread, brush) (b) green, grass (or grow, ground)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.
